title: bd dolt push fails 403: sync.remote points at upstream, not the fork
description: 'bd dolt push' fails with 'fatal: unable to access https://github.com/noshishiRust/leptos-daisyui-rs.git/: The requested URL returned error: 403'. Cause: .beads/config.yaml line 64 sets sync.remote to git+https://github.com/noshishiRust/leptos-daisyui-rs.git -- that is UPSTREAM (noshishiRust), which we have no write access to. This repo is an internal fork; the writable remote is 'fork' = https://github.com/davidcforbes/leptos-daisyui-rs.git. Consequence: beads state is not being backed up off-machine. Confirmed .beads/issues.jsonl is stale (23 issues, all closed, missing ldui-b08), so recent closures live only in the local Dolt DB and would be lost with the workstation. Not auto-fixed: repointing sync.remote decides where issue data gets published, which is a human call. Fix candidates: (a) bd config set sync.remote git+https://github.com/davidcforbes/leptos-daisyui-rs.git then bd dolt push; or (b) rely on the git-tracked .beads/issues.jsonl and get auto-flush/export working so closures land in commits.
acceptance_criteria: bd dolt push exits 0, OR .beads/issues.jsonl contains ldui-b08 as closed and is committed to the fork.
notes: ROOT CAUSE CORRECTED. Not sync.remote in config.yaml -- 'bd dolt push' never reads that key. The real setting is the DOLT remote: 'bd dolt remote list' showed origin -> git+https://github.com/noshishiRust/leptos-daisyui-rs.git (upstream, unwritable). Repointing sync.remote to the fork changed 'bd config get sync.remote' but the very next push still 403'd against upstream, which is what exposed the mistake. Fix applied: bd dolt remote remove origin; bd dolt remote add origin git+https://github.com/davidcforbes/leptos-daisyui-rs.git. Verified both the SQL-side view (bd dolt remote list) and the CLI-side view (dolt remote -v in .beads/dolt/ldui) agree, then 'bd dolt push' returned 'Push complete.' (exit 0). sync.remote was also left pointing at the fork -- harmless and directionally right. NOTE: 'bd dolt remote add' warns it only writes the SQL side; check the CLI side too. STILL OPEN and NOT fixed by this: .beads/issues.jsonl is stale (23 issues, all closed, missing ldui-b08), so the git-tracked JSONL export is not keeping up with the Dolt DB. Tracked separately in ldui-2ux.
close_reason: Fixed: the Dolt remote 'origin' pointed at upstream noshishiRust (unwritable). Removed and re-added it as git+https://github.com/davidcforbes/leptos-daisyui-rs.git; verified SQL-side and CLI-side views agree; 'bd dolt push' now returns 'Push complete.' (exit 0). The title's blame on sync.remote was wrong -- see notes. Residual stale-JSONL issue split out to ldui-izn.

title: .beads/issues.jsonl export is stale — closures live only in the local Dolt DB
description: The git-tracked .beads/issues.jsonl does not reflect the Dolt DB. It contains 23 issues, all status=closed, and does NOT contain ldui-b08 (closed 2026-07-10) or ldui-e8o (created 2026-07-10). So the JSONL export -- the git-backed recovery path -- has stopped keeping up with bd writes. Risk: if the local Dolt DB in .beads/dolt/ldui is lost, recent issue state is unrecoverable from git. 'bd dolt push' to the fork now works (see ldui-e8o), which mitigates but does not fix this: the JSONL is what a fresh clone reads. Investigate auto-flush (config: no-auto-flush, flush-debounce) and whether the pre-commit hook that used to run 'bd sync --flush-only' was disabled by the bd v1.0 upgrade that removed the 'bd sync' subcommand (see kv.memory.bd-v1-pre-commit-hook-fix -- that memory notes this repo's .git/hooks/pre-commit still has the bug and was never patched).

notes: DIAGNOSED, not fixed. 'bd export' itself works: a probe export to a temp file yields 77 issues (2 open, 75 closed) and DOES contain ldui-b08, ldui-e8o and ldui-izn. The tracked .beads/issues.jsonl has only 23 (all closed). So the export code path is healthy; what is broken is the auto-flush that should refresh the tracked file after mutations. Ruled out: the stale 'bd sync --flush-only' pre-commit hook theory -- core.hooksPath=.githooks, and no hook under .githooks/, .git/hooks/ or .beads/hooks/ references 'bd sync'. Deliberately NOT auto-fixed: overwriting issues.jsonl (23 -> 77 entries) at session end could disturb beads' import path, and off-machine durability is already restored now that 'bd dolt push' to the fork works (ldui-e8o). Next step: work out why auto-flush is not firing (config keys no-auto-flush / flush-debounce, and note .beads/beads.left.jsonl + export-state.json exist, suggesting a compaction/split scheme that may explain the 23-issue subset). Then run 'bd export --output .beads/issues.jsonl' and commit.

title: markdown ThemeContext signals disposed while global observer holds them (AiChat WASM panic)
description: Browser smoke (ldui-0wf) found: sending any message in the AiChat demo panics the whole WASM app: 'At src/markdown/theme.rs:46:34 you tried to access a reactive value defined at theme.rs:100:18 but it has already been disposed', followed by RuntimeError: unreachable and a follow-on 'RefCell already borrowed' panic. Root cause: use_theme() creates RwSignals owned by the first calling component's reactive owner (theme.rs:100-101) and registers them with install_theme_observer (global, once per document). AiChat rebuilds MessageBubble/MarkdownView on every poll tick, so the first bubble's owner is disposed while the global observer + subsequent palette() calls (theme.rs:46) still reference the dead signals. Fix: give ThemeContext signals document lifetime (create under a detached/leaked root owner or thread_local singleton), independent of any component scope.
close_reason: Both fixed in 05260cd and verified live in the browser smoke session. ldui-i4t: ThemeContext is now a thread_local document-lifetime singleton whose signals are created under a deliberately parentless leaked Owner (document_root_owner via Owner unset/new/set), so the global MutationObserver can't outlive them — AiChat send no longer panics; reviewer verified the ownership trick against reactive_graph 0.2.14 source; regression test added in 44d7c52. ldui-4i0: performance.memory now read as a property via js_sys::Reflect::get (Performance web-sys feature added) — no more per-tick TypeError. title: AiChat auto-scroll reads stale scroll_height, leaves latest message below fold
description: Browser smoke (ldui-0wf) confirmed the Task 19 deferred auto-scroll concern is a real bug. Repro: AiChat demo, stick engaged (scrolled to bottom), send a message. The reply arrives (bubbles 2->4, scrollHeight 352->733) but scrollTop lands at 267 while the true bottom is scrollHeight-clientHeight = 496 — ~230px of the newest content stays below the fold, and it never corrects. Also on the very first message: scrollHeight 352 vs clientHeight 237 (115px overflow) but scrollTop stays 0. Root cause: the auto-stick Effect at src/components/ai_chat/component.rs:183-191 calls el.set_scroll_top(el.scroll_height()) synchronously when  changes, but Leptos Effects run after the reactive update and BEFORE the browser lays out the newly-appended MessageBubble DOM, so scroll_height() is stale (too small). The stale programmatic scroll can also trip the on:scroll handler (component.rs:209-216) into recomputing should_stick_to_bottom with a large distance, flipping stick=false and disengaging future auto-scroll (explains scrollTop stuck at 0 on first send). Fix: defer the scroll to after paint — request_animation_frame (web_sys) before reading scroll_height and setting scroll_top, or set_timeout(0). The pure should_stick_to_bottom logic is correct and well-tested; the bug is purely the measurement timing in the Effect. NOTE: P1 theme panic (ldui-i4t) and P3 memory error (ldui-4i0) were both verified FIXED live in this same session — console is clean, no more disposal panic.
close_reason: Fixed in 3b600d4: deferred the auto-stick scroll write into a request_animation_frame callback (leptos::prelude::request_animation_frame, one-shot per Effect run, None-guarded) so it reads scroll_height AFTER the browser paints the new bubbles. Re-verified live on rebuilt WASM (a86fe2309...): after 1st message distance-from-bottom=0 (was 115px overflow at scrollTop 0); after 2nd message scrollTop 497 of 733, distance -1≈0 (was 267/dist 229 below fold). title: Integrate ui-tokens shared crate into leptos-daisyui-rs
description:
Bring in the shared `ui-tokens` crate from the Rust-DeskApp workspace so leptos-daisyui-rs consumes the same design tokens (durations, easings, shadow elevation tiers, colour palette anchors) as d2d-ui. This is the prerequisite for the motion-port epic (ldui-e1o) — without a single source of truth for motion durations and shadow tiers, every component-level port would have to redefine the same constants and the libraries would drift.

## Why now

The d2d-ui motion epic (Rust-DeskApp/beads-14f) shipped 2026-05 with a complete `ui_tokens::motion` (Easing enum, DURATION_FAST_MS/DURATION_NORMAL_MS, cubic-Bezier control points) and `ui_tokens::elevation` (LEVEL_2..LEVEL_64 Shadow structs). The motion-port epic (ldui-e1o) is parked until this anchor is in place.

## Decision: path-dep vs git-dep vs vendored

The original parity epic (beads-76r) flagged this as needing a "path-dep decision". Three options:

1. **Path-dep** (`ui-tokens = { path = "../Rust-DeskApp/crates/ui-tokens" }`) — cleanest while both repos are local. Breaks for downstream crates.io consumers and for CI without sibling-repo checkout.
2. **Git-dep** (`ui-tokens = { git = "https://github.com/davidcforbes/rust-deskapp", branch = "master" }`) — works for crates.io publication and CI. Slower (git fetch on each build). Pinning to a commit hash recommended.
3. **Vendored copy** — manual sync. Drift-prone but simple.

Recommended: git-dep with a pinned commit hash. Migrate to path-dep only for local development if needed.

## Surface to consume

From the d2d-ui ui-tokens crate (C:\dev\Rust-DeskApp\crates\ui-tokens\src\):

- `motion.rs` — `Easing { Linear, Standard, Decelerate, Accelerate }`, `DURATION_FAST_MS`, `DURATION_NORMAL_MS`, cubic-Bezier control points
- `elevation.rs` — `Shadow { offset_x, offset_y, blur, opacity }`, named tiers `LEVEL_2`/`LEVEL_4`/`LEVEL_8`/`LEVEL_16`/`LEVEL_64`
- `colour.rs` / `theme.rs` (if applicable to web) — accent + neutral palette anchors

## How web consumes these (translation strategy)

- Emit motion constants as `--ld-duration-fast: 83ms; --ld-duration-normal: 200ms;` CSS variables in a token preamble (build-time, via a small leptos-side helper).
- Easing cubic-Bezier control points emit as `cubic-bezier(...)` CSS easing functions.
- Elevation shadows emit as `box-shadow: <offset_x>px <offset_y>px <blur>px rgba(0,0,0,<opacity>);` per tier.
- Colour palette consumed via existing daisyUI theme infrastructure.

## Verification

- New crate dependency builds clean (`cargo build`, `cargo test` from leptos-daisyui-rs root).
- Token preamble CSS emitted from a small `ui_tokens_css!()` macro or build.rs.
- At least one component (Button is the obvious candidate) uses one motion token (e.g., `--ld-duration-fast` for hover transition) to prove the chain.

## Unblocks

- ldui-e1o (motion + shadow system port) — explicitly blocked-by-convention on this bead.
close_reason: Implemented in 305c551: ui-tokens path dep + tokens module + UiTokensPreamble + demo inspection page. 1154 tests pass, wasm32 build clean.

title: Port d2d-ui motion + shadow system to leptos-daisyui-rs
description:
Epic to port the motion + drop-shadow system shipped in the d2d-ui Rust-DeskApp workspace (beads-14f, merged 2026-05) across to leptos-daisyui-rs. Cross-stack flow:

  d2d-ui (Direct2D, native) -> leptos-daisyui-rs (Leptos/WASM, CSS) -> table-rs (sibling effort, separate epic)

## Why

d2d-ui's beads-14f epic shipped a complete motion system: eased hover/press/focus, ripple reveals, elevation lift on hover, GPU drop shadows via CLSID_D2D1Shadow, dialog scale-up + backdrop fade, toast slide-in, menu/dropdown/drawer entrances. ~70 controls migrated. The patterns are now battle-tested in native code. Bringing them to the web library accelerates app development by sharing the same visual language across renderers.

## Scope

Port these motion patterns to their CSS / Web Animations API equivalents:

- Eased state transitions (cubic-Bezier hover/press/focus opacity + scale + colour)
- Ripple click reveal (radial expanding overlay)
- Elevation lift (shadow + slight translate on hover for Card / Fab)
- Drop shadows (CSS filter: drop-shadow or box-shadow per elevation tier)
- Dialog entrance: scale 0.92 -> 1.0 + backdrop fade-in
- Toast entrance: slide-in from corner
- Menu / dropdown / drawer slide-down or edge-slide
- Focus ring animated fade-in + outset

## Source of truth (d2d-ui side)

- `crates/d2d-ui/src/motion/` -- clock, easing, transition, spring, ripple, StateAnim
- `crates/d2d-ui/src/shadow.rs` -- CLSID_D2D1Shadow wrapper + ui_tokens::elevation::Shadow
- `crates/ui-tokens/src/motion.rs` -- Easing enum + DURATION_FAST_MS / DURATION_NORMAL_MS
- `crates/ui-tokens/src/elevation.rs` -- LEVEL_2 / LEVEL_4 / LEVEL_8 / LEVEL_16 / LEVEL_64 shadow tiers
- `docs/components/motion.md` -- reference doc

## Anchor on ui-tokens (depends on ldui-wab)

This epic depends on the ui-tokens integration tracked under ldui-wab. Once leptos-daisyui-rs consumes the shared ui-tokens crate, motion durations + shadow tiers automatically stay in sync with d2d-ui via a single source of truth. Without that anchor, this port would drift.

## Suggested fan-out (children to file when work starts)

1. ui-tokens integration (already tracked: ldui-wab)
2. Eased button hover/press/focus -- the universal interaction pattern
3. Eased checkbox / toggle / radio interaction
4. Card elevation lift (LEVEL_4 -> LEVEL_8 on hover)
5. Ripple effect on click (radial overlay)
6. Dialog scale-up + backdrop fade-in
7. Toast slide-in entrance from corner
8. Menu / dropdown slide-down entrance
9. Drawer edge-slide entrance
10. Focus ring animated fade-in

## Out of scope (this epic)

- Porting to table-rs -- separate sibling epic when ready
- Wholesale rewrite of existing leptos-daisyui-rs components -- this is additive
- Reactive signal redesign -- continue using existing Leptos signal patterns

## Related

- d2d-ui motion epic: Rust-DeskApp/beads-14f (closed 2026-05)
- d2d-ui WinUI 3 reference: Rust-DeskApp/beads-v3f, beads-n5a (closed 2026-05)
- Leptos parity epic: ldui parity epic (open)

title: Add multi-select to DataTable for parity with d2d-ui (Rust-DeskApp)
description:
Rust-DeskApp commit c5bdfa9 added multi-select to d2d_ui::controls::DataTable so desktop apps can support Ctrl/Shift-click row selection. The Leptos DataTable currently has no selection state.

Gap: To keep desktop ↔ web feature parity (per Rust-DeskApp/docs/leptos-parity.md), add equivalent multi-select to leptos-daisyui-rs's DataTable.

Proposed API (Leptos signal-based):
  - new optional prop: selected_rows: RwSignal<BTreeSet<usize>>
  - new optional prop: selection_anchor: RwSignal<Option<usize>>
  - new optional prop: on_row_click: Callback<(usize, MouseEvent)>
  - DataTableBody renders selected rows with class 'bg-base-200' (or similar)
  - Pure logic helper: pub fn handle_row_click(row_idx, ctrl, shift, &mut selected, &mut anchor, total) — mirrors d2d-ui's same-named method. Consumers can wire up MouseEvent.ctrl_key() / shift_key() to call it.

Reference: d2d-ui implementation at crates/d2d-ui/src/controls/data_table.rs handle_row_click — same semantics:
  - plain click: clear, select clicked, set anchor
  - Ctrl+click: toggle, set anchor
  - Shift+click: range from anchor (clears unless Ctrl held)

Clearing selection on page change / data refresh / sort change is also expected.

When complete, update Rust-DeskApp/docs/leptos-parity.md to mark this row from ❌ to ✅.

title: TextRotate: rotating words render above the baseline and are clipped (mostly invisible)
description: User-reported (2026-07-08), confirmed LIVE on /components/text_rotate. The rotating words are almost entirely invisible/clipped: e.g. 'Hello, I'm [blank]', 'Our product is [blank] and loved by developers worldwide' — the animated word area shows nothing or a sliver. Measured live: the .text-rotate > span > span items render with their tops ~80-164px ABOVE the .text-rotate box top (all items overflowsTop:true), and the box computes overflow:hidden with height == line-height (e.g. 40px for text-4xl), so the items are positioned outside the visible band and clipped away. Even the resting first-child (opacity 1, translateY 0) is not visible. Root cause is the component's positioning model in demo/custom-components.css lines 139-161: .text-rotate (relative, inline-block), middle .text-rotate>span (relative, inline-block, no height), items .text-rotate>span>span (absolute, top:0 left:0). The absolute items are not aligned to the text baseline and the container does not establish a correct visible band, so with the translateY(0 -> -20px) keyframes the text renders above the line. NOTE: source .text-rotate rule sets NO overflow, yet it computes overflow:hidden — track down where that comes from (possibly a Tailwind utility or inherited rule) as part of the fix. FIX (needs iterative CSS rework, not a one-liner): rebuild the container as a fixed-height overflow-hidden band with items vertically stacked and animating within it, aligned to baseline; verify each of the 6 demo examples shows the rotating word fully. Component: src/components/text_rotate/component.rs (markup) + demo/custom-components.css (.text-rotate rules + text-rotate-N-items keyframes). P3 visual.
close_reason: Fixed in 67f768e. Rewrote .text-rotate CSS (demo/custom-components.css) from a broken absolute/relative model to an inline-grid stack: display:contents on the middle span flattens it so items become grid children of .text-rotate, all sharing grid cell 1/1 (overlap in place), box sizes to widest word, visible word sits on the text baseline. Root cause was the old middle container computing to ~3 line-heights (120px), pushing items ~80px above the visible band where overflow clipped them. Verified live on the rebuilt artifact across all 6 demo examples: every visible word visInBand:true + box alignedToLine:true; animation cycles one word at a time correctly.

title: Hover3d: flicker on hover + cards overlap section headers
description:
User-reported (2026-07-08), two bugs on the Hover 3D demo page, both rooted in demo/custom-components.css .hover-3d (lines 256-284) + src/components/hover_3d/component.rs.

ISSUE 1 — FLICKER while hovering (even mouse ~stationary). Diagnosed LIVE with event counters: with a truly stationary cursor, ZERO mouse events fire over 2s and transform stays flat, and during movement each mousemove produces exactly one clean transform write (no cascade). So it is NOT a JS mousemove/mouseleave feedback loop. Root cause is GPU 3D compositing / z-fighting: .hover-3d sets transform-style:preserve-3d + perspective:1000px (lines 258-259) and hosts 8 empty hover-zone divs at z-index:10, pointer-events:all (lines 269-275) that are COPLANAR in that same 3D context with the tilted content child; the content also has transition:transform 0.1s (line 265). Once any tilt is applied (any hover), the coplanar zone overlay and the perspective-projected card surface z-fight and the compositor repaints every frame = visible flicker. Real-mouse micro-jitter + the 0.1s transition adds a jello wobble on top.
FIX options (pick minimal): (a) take the hover content out of coplanar conflict / promote it to its own layer — e.g. give the content will-change:transform or translateZ(0), or wrap the tilt target in an inner element isolated from the zones; (b) set pointer-events:none on the tilting content so only the (non-moving) zones+host do hit-testing; (c) drop transform-style:preserve-3d on the content children (they have no 3D children) and/or remove the 0.1s transition so tilt is instant. Verify live that flicker stops.

ISSUE 2 — cards OVERLAP the section header above them. Measured LIVE (static, NOT tilt-related — max up-tilt moves card only ~1px): the .hover-3d host box is SHORTER than its card content and centers the overflow, so the card bleeds ~10-22px ABOVE the host top into the preceding h2. E.g. Credit Card host height 224px vs card content 269px -> card top 22px above host; card top 382 vs 'Credit Card Style' h2 bottom 388 = 6px overlap; Product Showcase cards 11px over their h2. Host computes display:grid with a track shorter than content (source not in the .hover-3d rule as read — implementer should pin where display:grid/height comes from: a Tailwind class, the Card, or an inherited rule). FIX: make .hover-3d size to its content (height:auto / min-content, or align/justify so the card doesn't overflow the track), OR add adequate top spacing so the 3D card cannot collide with the header. Verify the card no longer touches the h2 above at rest.

Both fixes land in demo/custom-components.css and possibly src/components/hover_3d/component.rs. Low priority visual polish, but user-visible. NOTE during repro the MCP browser tab kept auto-drifting between hover_3d/hover_gallery/icon_tile — that was tooling confusion with multiple tabs, not a product routing bug (hover_3d loads fine on direct nav).
close_reason: Fixed in 5716a32 (demo/custom-components.css). OVERLAP: verified FIXED (measured + visual on rebuilt artifact). The perspective-projected card rendered ~10-27px outside its host box and collided with the section header above; added margin-block:1.5rem so the tilt has breathing room — card-top-to-header gaps went from -6..-11px (overlapping) to +13..+18px (clear); confirmed visually (Basic/Credit Card/Product Showcase all have clear space below their headers). FLICKER: changed the tilted content from transform-style:preserve-3d to flat — it removes the content from a shared 3D context coplanar with the z-index:10 hover-zone overlay (the diagnosed GPU z-fighting/repaint cause) while the tilt still works (verified: rotateX/Y still renders as matrix3d via the host's inherited perspective). CAVEAT: the flicker is a compositing repaint that only manifests with real-mouse hover (0 JS events fire on a stationary CDP cursor), so I could not reproduce it headlessly to confirm the fix eliminates it — needs user confirmation with a real mouse; reopen if it persists.
